explanations.answer: So the Son may glorify the Father
explanations.explanation: Jesus asks, “Glorify Your Son, that Your Son may glorify You.” Look at where that lands, friend. The honor goes right back to the Father. Jesus asks, and the Father ends up with the glory.

explanations.answer: So the crowds will follow the Son
explanations.explanation: No crowds show up in this prayer at all. Jesus says, “…that Your Son may glorify You.” The reason points to the Father, not to anybody following along. I get why you'd guess it, though. I count heads every time a batch comes out of the oven.

explanations.answer: So the disciples will stop worrying
explanations.explanation: Worry isn't the reason Jesus gives in verse 1. He says, “…that Your Son may glorify You.” The prayer does turn to the disciples a little later, but not here. This request is about the Son and the Father.

Jesus says the Father granted Him authority over all people “…so that He may give eternal life to all those You have given Him.” That's the gift the verse names. It's a good one, baker. Eternal life is what Jesus gives.

Money never comes up in this verse. The text says Jesus gives eternal life to all those the Father has given Him. I came with a 25 cent price sticker, so I understand the wishful thinking. Wealth just isn't the gift here.

Authority over all people sounds like a throne, I know. But verse 2 says what Jesus does with it: He gives eternal life to all those the Father has given Him. No earthly kingdom is mentioned in that verse. The gift is eternal life.

explanations.answer: Knowing the only true God and Jesus Christ
explanations.explanation: Jesus says, “Now this is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent.” He explains eternal life as knowing the Father and the Son. That's the whole definition He gives right there in the prayer.

explanations.answer: Living forever without ever growing old
explanations.explanation: Jesus doesn't talk about growing old here, friend. He says eternal life is “…that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent.” It's about knowing God and Jesus Christ. Nobody is handing out a number to live up to in verse 3.

explanations.answer: Keeping every law without one slip
explanations.explanation: Laws and slips don't come up in this verse. Jesus says eternal life is “…that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent.” That's knowing, not a perfect record. Nobody is graded on a clipboard in verse 3.
Jesus says, “I have glorified You on earth by accomplishing the work You gave Me to do.” The Father gave Him work, and He accomplished it. Nice and plain.
I can see why a journey would come to mind. But Jesus says He accomplished “…the work You gave Me to do.” The word is work, not journey. Journey just isn't in the verse.

Battle sounds dramatic, I'll give you that. The only battle I've ever fought is a cookie stuck in my stamp, and the cookie won. Jesus says He glorified the Father by accomplishing “…the work You gave Me to do.”

I get the thought, since Jesus does ask for glory. But He asks for “…the glory I had with You before the world existed.” That glory isn't new to Him. He had it with the Father before the world existed.

Jesus asks the Father, “…glorify Me in Your presence with the glory I had with You before the world existed.” Look at that word "had." He isn't asking for something brand new, friend. He's asking to be back in the Father's presence with the glory that was already His, like a stamper asking for his own spot on the counter.
Jesus says of the disciples, “They were Yours; You gave them to Me, and they have kept Your word.” They kept it. Hold onto that word, friend, because it's the one Jesus uses.
Forgetting is the opposite of what Jesus says. He says, “…they have kept Your word.” I know a little about being forgotten, and I'm glad it's not in this verse.
Doubt isn't what Jesus says about them here. He says, “…they have kept Your word.” They were the Father's, the Father gave them to Jesus, and they kept the word.

explanations.answer: That Jesus came from the Father
explanations.explanation: Jesus says, “They knew with certainty that I came from You, and they believed that You sent Me.” That's what they knew for sure. They had received the words He gave them, and they knew where He came from.

explanations.answer: That they would never be scattered
explanations.explanation: Nothing about being scattered shows up in this verse. Jesus says of the disciples, “They knew with certainty that I came from You, and they believed that You sent Me.” That's what they knew with certainty. Scattering isn't part of it.

explanations.answer: That Jesus would be crowned king soon
explanations.explanation: A crown isn't mentioned in this verse, friend. Jesus says they “…knew with certainty that I came from You, and they believed that You sent Me.” That's their certainty. Nothing about timing or crowns.

Jesus says, “I do not ask on behalf of the world, but on behalf of those You have given Me; for they are Yours.” Here He's asking on behalf of the ones the Father gave Him. The world is the one He names as not included in this request.
Angels aren't mentioned in verse 9 at all. Jesus says, “I do not ask on behalf of the world, but on behalf of those You have given Me…” The world is the one He says He isn't asking for here.
Priests don't appear in this verse. The one Jesus names is the world: “I do not ask on behalf of the world…” He's asking on behalf of those the Father gave Him, because they are the Father's.

Jesus says, “Holy Father, protect them by Your name, the name You gave Me, so that they may be one as We are one.” Protection comes with a purpose, and the purpose is oneness. That word is going to come up again before this prayer is over.

Jesus doesn't say that. He says, “…protect them by Your name, the name You gave Me, so that they may be one as We are one.” In fact, a few verses later He says the world has hated them. Protection here is for oneness.

explanations.answer: So they may rule the nations
explanations.explanation: Ruling isn't what this verse is about. Jesus asks the Father to protect them “…so that they may be one as We are one.” The goal is oneness, friend, not a throne.
Jesus says, “Not one of them has been lost, except the son of destruction, so that the Scripture would be fulfilled.” He protected and preserved them by the Father's name. Lost is the word He uses.
Chosen is a good word, but it isn't the one in this verse. Jesus says, “Not one of them has been lost, except the son of destruction…” The word is lost.
Sent does show up in this prayer, just later. In verse 18 Jesus says, “…I have also sent them into the world.” But verse 12 says, “Not one of them has been lost, except the son of destruction…”

Jesus says the son of destruction was lost “…so that the Scripture would be fulfilled.” He doesn't say which Scripture in this prayer, so I won't guess. He just says Scripture, and that's where we stop.
Angels don't appear in this verse. Jesus says it happened “…so that the Scripture would be fulfilled.” Scripture is what He names.
No priest and no vow in verse 12, friend. What Jesus says is fulfilled is “the Scripture.” He doesn't name a passage here, so I'll leave it right there.

explanations.answer: So His joy may be fulfilled in them
explanations.explanation: Jesus says, “…I am saying these things while I am in the world, so that they may have My joy fulfilled within them.” He's still in the world as He prays. The reason He gives is joy, and it's His joy.

explanations.answer: So they will remember His words
explanations.explanation: Remembering sounds sensible, and I forget where I put my own hat. But that isn't the reason Jesus gives. He says He's saying these things “…so that they may have My joy fulfilled within them.”

explanations.answer: So the priests cannot accuse Him
explanations.explanation: No priests appear in this verse. Jesus gives His reason plainly: “…so that they may have My joy fulfilled within them.” It's about the disciples having His joy.
Jesus says, “I have given them Your word and the world has hated them.” He tells it to the Father straight. And He follows it with, “For they are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.”
Honor would be nice, friend, but it isn't what Jesus says. His words are, “…the world has hated them.” He follows with “For they are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.”
Ignoring would almost be a mercy next to what Jesus says. His words are, “…the world has hated them.” That's the word He uses, and He says it to the Father.

explanations.answer: That the Father keep them from the evil one
explanations.explanation: Jesus says, “I am not asking that You take them out of the world, but that You keep them from the evil one.” He isn't asking for them to be taken out of the world. His request is that the Father keep them from the evil one.

explanations.answer: That the Father make them powerful in it
explanations.explanation: Power isn't what Jesus asks for. He says, “I am not asking that You take them out of the world, but that You keep them from the evil one.” That's the request, and it's about being kept.

explanations.answer: That the Father hide them away for a while
explanations.explanation: I'd hide in my own oven if I could fit, friend. But Jesus says, “I am not asking that You take them out of the world…” What He asks for is “…that You keep them from the evil one.”
Jesus says, “Sanctify them by the truth; Your word is truth.” He is asking the Father to sanctify them by the truth. And He says the Father's word is truth.
The temple is a fair guess, but it isn't in this verse. Jesus says, “Your word is truth.” The truth is the Father's word.
Kingdom doesn't show up in verse 17. Jesus says, “Sanctify them by the truth; Your word is truth.” The blank is word.
Jesus says, “As You sent Me into the world, I have also sent them into the world.” The Father sent Jesus, and Jesus has sent the disciples. It's the same kind of sending, said in one line.
Jesus actually does say it. Verse 18 reads, “As You sent Me into the world, I have also sent them into the world.” So the disciples are sent too.

explanations.answer: Those who will believe through their message
explanations.explanation: Jesus says, “I am not asking on behalf of them alone, but also on behalf of those who will believe in Me through their message…” The prayer reaches past the disciples to people who believe through their message. That's a wide circle, friend, and Jesus prays for it.

explanations.answer: Those who will reject their message
explanations.explanation: Verse 20 names the opposite group. Jesus is asking on behalf of “…those who will believe in Me through their message…” It doesn't mention people who reject it.

explanations.answer: Those who will rule over their nation
explanations.explanation: Rulers don't come up in this verse. Jesus prays for “…those who will believe in Me through their message…” That's who He adds to the prayer.

explanations.answer: So the world may believe the Father sent Him
explanations.explanation: Jesus prays, “May they also be in Us, so that the world may believe that You sent Me.” Oneness is tied to the world believing. That's the reason He gives.

explanations.answer: So they can outnumber all their enemies
explanations.explanation: Numbers aren't the point of this verse. Jesus says oneness is “…so that the world may believe that You sent Me.” No enemies are counted.

explanations.answer: So they will never have to disagree
explanations.explanation: I've never even agreed with my own mustache about where the flour goes. But verse 21 says nothing about disagreeing. Jesus prays for oneness “…so that the world may believe that You sent Me.”

Jesus prays for them to be perfectly united “…so that the world may know that You sent Me and have loved them just as You have loved Me.” There are two things for the world to know. The Father sent Jesus, and the Father has loved them just as He has loved Jesus.

It's in there, friend. Jesus says, “…so that the world may know that You sent Me and have loved them just as You have loved Me.” So He prays that the world may know about the Father's love for them too.

explanations.answer: To be with Him where He is
explanations.explanation: Jesus says, “Father, I want those You have given Me to be with Me where I am, that they may see the glory You gave Me…” He wants them with Him. He also wants them to see His glory.
Jerusalem doesn't come up in this prayer. Jesus says He wants those the Father gave Him “…to be with Me where I am…” That's where He wants them.

explanations.answer: To go back home to Galilee
explanations.explanation: Galilee, a region of Israel, isn't mentioned in this prayer. What Jesus wants is for them “…to be with Me where I am…” That's the wish He tells the Father.

Jesus says the Father gave Him glory “…because You loved Me before the foundation of the world.” So He places the Father's love for Him before the foundation of the world, not at His coming into it. That's the part to hold onto, baker.

Jesus says the Father gave Him glory “…because You loved Me before the foundation of the world.” The Father's love didn't start when Jesus came into the world. It was there before the foundation of the world.
Close, since Jesus does say He has made the name known. But He keeps going: “…I have made Your name known to them and will continue to make it known…” So He isn't done.
Jesus says, “…I have made Your name known to them and will continue to make it known…” Past and future in one breath. He has done it, and He will keep doing it.

explanations.answer: So the Father's love for Him may be in them
explanations.explanation: Jesus says He'll keep making the name known “…so that the love You have for Me may be in them, and I in them.” The Father's love for Jesus in them, and Jesus in them. That's how the prayer ends.

explanations.answer: So the whole world will fear the Father
explanations.explanation: Fear isn't what verse 26 says. Jesus says He'll keep making the name known “…so that the love You have for Me may be in them, and I in them.” The reason is love.

explanations.answer: So the disciples can win every argument
explanations.explanation: I've never won an argument with a bowl of cookie dough, so I won't promise it for anybody else. Verse 26 says no such thing. Jesus keeps making the name known “…so that the love You have for Me may be in them, and I in them.”
